summary: Intermittent dedicated throughput degradation caused by oscillatory fanout and prefetch shadowing
summary_details: Customer reports periodic p99/p50 throughput collapse on their dedicated pool. Symptoms include a rapid surge in attach latency and a subsequent drop in steady-state batch throughput; GPU attach failures surface as 502/504 from the customer-facing routes before autoscaler kicks in.
description:
Issue summary:
- Observed: recurring throughput dips for CobaltAI's dedicated pool starting 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC. Pattern: short (2-8 minute) windows of high attach latency and increased 5xx, followed by partial recovery.
Impact:
- Customer facing: up to 40% reduction in effective token/sec for several production routes; increased tail latency for synchronous endpoints.
- Business: Dedicated customer (paid SLA) experiencing missed SLOs and degraded user experience.
Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-13 (NVIDIA H100 mix), Node image 2026-02-28, runtime v2.11.3.
Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Normal steady traffic; 2) sudden fanout across many short-lived streams (chatlets) triggered by customer load generator; 3) allocator shows many small slot reservations; 4) prefetch subsystem grows KV-cache entries for ephemeral contexts; 5) attach latency spikes, requests time out / return 5xx; 6) autoscaler starts to add nodes but partial capacity mismatch causes transient GPU scarcity.
Logs / metrics collected:
- Grafana: dashboard dp-us-east-13/pool-overview shows p95 attach latency spike from 120ms to 2.8s at 09:12.
- Allocator logs: repeated "slot_acquire_timeout" with correlated tenant_id.
- Serving runtime logs: "prefetch_incomplete" warnings and "kv_cache_pressure" metrics rising by 6x.
- Nginx / gateway: increased 502/504 for routes /v1/generate-chat and /v1/stream.
Initial triage notes:
- Hypothesis A: no single GPU failure; rather a noisy-tenant microburst (many short-lived streams) causing slot fragmentation and prefetch growth that starves longer batched requests.
- Hypothesis B: autoscaler hysteresis + node initialization lag produces a short window of real GPU scarcity because new nodes are not provisioned with the warmed KV-cache / prefetch state.
- Hypothesis C: a sidecar telemetry spike triggered background IO (snapshotter) increasing PCIe latency in a subset of nodes.
Workaround given to customer:
- Temporary mitigation: reduce chatlet concurrency (client-side knob) and increase keepalive to consolidate streams. We advised routing heavy short-request loads to a lower-priority route that uses a smaller-context variant of the model.
Next steps:
- SRE to run "prefetch-snapshot" diagnostic and capture KV-cache growth traces for the time window.
- Engineering to validate autoscaler cooldown thresholds and warmup policies for dedicated pools.
- If confirmed noisy-tenant, consider short-term weight-based throttling at the pool ingress for the tenant.
- Notify CobaltAI CS and schedule a joint test window for tuned concurrency settings.

2026-03-10 09:45 - Liam O'Connor: Observed allocator slot_acquire_timeouts coincident with attach latency spikes. Spawned live trace for tenant_id=cobalt-42.
2026-03-10 10:10 - SRE (Maya Chen): Confirmed no GPU hardware alerts; PCIe error counters normal on affected hosts. Noted spike in snapshotter io ops on 3/8 nodes.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Backend Eng (Erik Svensson): Reproduced small-fanout workload in staging; reproduced KV-cache growth pattern and attach latency increase when many ephemeral streams created concurrently.
2026-03-11 02:30 - Observability (Priya Rao): Added temporary alert for kv_cache_pressure > 3x baseline for any dedicated pool. Linked alert to SUP-2755552.

2026-03-11 09:00 - Liam O'Connor: Ran mitigations: increased autoscaler aggressive_coldstart=true in a single test pool; observed faster node additions but p99 still impacted due to cold KV cache state.
2026-03-12 08:15 - Engineering: Started design doc for short-term ingress throttling mechanism and model-variant fallback to reduce bursty small-stream load on dedicated pools.
2026-03-12 12:00 - Customer (CobaltAI - ops@cobalt.ai): Confirmed they applied reduced concurrency and reported partial improvement (p50 restored, p99 still elevated during peaks).
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10 09:25: Thanks for the details — we're treating this as P1. Assigned to SRE oncall.

Maya Chen (SRE) 2026-03-10 09:50: No host-level GPU faults found. Collecting allocator traces and prefetch metrics. See slack thread #support-cobaltai (https://slack.redwood/support-cobaltai/p123456).

Erik Svensson (Backend) 2026-03-10 11:15: Repro in staging: creating many 50-200ms chatlets causes prefetch table to grow ~4x and fragments slots. Patch idea: enforce min-duration for ephemeral reservations or consolidate by tenant id. Filing followup INT ticket.
CobaltAI (Customer) 2026-03-10 12:02: We'll throttle chatlets from our side tonight and report back. Appreciate the quick triage.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-11 09:05: Temporary autoscaler tweak applied to test pool. Need engineering to evaluate warm-cache strategies.
resolution_notes: (in progress) Short-term customer-side throttle reduced impact. Engineering to implement ingress fairness and consider pre-warming KV cache on autoscale. No permanent fix deployed yet.
postmortem_followup_items: Design and land ingress tenant-weighted rate limiter for dedicated pools (ENG-alloc-2347)
Autoscaler: add warmup hook to pre-populate KV cache for new nodes or use fast snapshot restore (ENG-autoscale-451)
Add metric: tenant_prefetch_growth and alert on >3x baseline during peak windows (OBS-98)
CS: create customer guide for tuning chatlet concurrency and keepalive settings (DOCS-22)
